featured.title: OpenAI Just Offered the US Government a 5% Stake. It Wants Every AI Company to Do the Same.
featured.excerpt: Sam Altman has pitched Trump, Bernie Sanders, and the Treasury Secretary on a sovereign wealth fund seeded by AI equity. Anthropic says it's not interested.
featured.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman at a meeting in February 2025
featured.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI professionals face equity dilution; White House AI advisor Sriram Krishnan is central to the talks; India's sovereign AI ambitions must now account for partially government-owned American competitors.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: CRED's Kunal Shah Is Now Running WhatsApp. Meta Paid $900 Million to Make It Happen.
news.excerpt: The Indian founder who turned credit card bills into a fintech empire now leads the world's biggest messaging app. It's the most consequential Indian tech appointment since Satya Nadella.
news.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED and newly appointed global head of WhatsApp (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: An Indian founder — not an Indian-American corporate executive — now leads the platform that is the primary communication channel between the diaspora and home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Has Now Served Notices to Every Major Messaging App Over Usernames. The Crackdown Is Widening.
news.excerpt: After freezing WhatsApp's username rollout, the government is now demanding answers from Telegram and Signal. Indian platform Arattai has already surrendered the feature entirely.
news.image_caption: A user texting on WhatsApp, India's dominant messaging platform with over 500 million users
news.nri_angle: Diaspora Indians who rely on WhatsApp, Telegram, and Signal to communicate with family could see privacy features limited if India forces platforms to tie usernames to verified phone numbers.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Opened Its Nuclear Sector to Private Money for the First Time in Sixty Years. The $214 Billion Race Is On.
news.excerpt: The SHANTI Act lets Adani, Tata, and Jindal build nuclear power plants. IIT Bombay is already training the engineers. And the West is watching closely.
news.image_caption: The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu, India's largest nuclear power station
news.nri_angle: The 49% FDI window means diaspora-led investment and Indian-origin nuclear engineers at US firms like Westinghouse now have a professional pathway into India's nuclear sector.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Refiners Are Redrawing the Oil Map. The Iran War Forced Their Hand.
news.excerpt: Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL are eyeing crude from Guyana, Brazil and the US to reduce their dependence on the Middle East — a shift that could be the most significant in India's energy history.
news.image_caption: An oil refinery in India — the country's refiners are reshaping crude supply chains after the Iran war disrupted Gulf shipping routes (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: India's crude oil import bill is the single biggest variable in the country's fiscal equation — affecting the rupee, inflation, petrol prices and government spending capacity. A structural shift in sourcing from the Gulf to the Americas and Africa would reshape India's economic risk profile for years.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's GST Revenue Just Hit ₹1.95 Lakh Crore in a Single Month. The Real Story Is in the Imports.
news.excerpt: Gross collections rose 14% year-on-year in June, powered by a 35% spike in import-linked taxes — a signal of surging trade that cuts both ways for the economy.
news.image_caption: India's GST collections have become a key barometer of economic health
news.nri_angle: GST collections are the most reliable real-time measure of India's economic health — the June numbers show both steady domestic consumption and a massive ramp-up in capital goods imports as global firms build manufacturing and data infrastructure.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Just Added Its Fewest Jobs Since February. India’s IT Stocks Are Rallying.
news.excerpt: The U.S. economy created only 57,000 jobs in June — roughly half what Wall Street expected. The weak print has pushed back rate-hike fears, sent the dollar tumbling, and given Indian markets their strongest week in months.
news.image_caption: The trading floor at the New York Stock Exchange on Wall Street
news.nri_angle: The weak U.S. jobs report eases rate-hike fears, stabilises the rupee, and lifts Indian IT stocks — directly affecting NRI employment prospects, mortgage costs, and the India-vs-America career calculus.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Delhi Just Banned New Petrol Two-Wheelers From 2028. No Indian City Has Gone This Far.
news.excerpt: India’s capital has launched its most aggressive electric vehicle policy yet — ₹15,000 crore in incentives, 30,000 new charging points, and a hard deadline that will force every new scooter buyer to go electric within two years.
news.image_caption: An electric vehicle charging station at NITI Aayog in New Delhi
news.nri_angle: Delhi’s EV push could improve the air quality that keeps NRIs from moving back, while opening investment opportunities in India’s booming electric vehicle supply chain.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: HCLTech Just Landed a $1.14 Billion AI Deal With a European Giant. It's the Biggest New Contract in Years.
news.excerpt: The Noida-headquartered IT services firm will build an AI-driven operating model for a major unnamed European company — entirely new business, not a renewal.
news.image_caption: HCLTech CEO C Vijayakumar, who has steered the company's pivot toward AI-led transformation services
news.nri_angle: HCLTech employs tens of thousands of Indian-origin engineers in the US and Europe — a mega deal of this size signals continued demand for Indian tech talent globally.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Sending Its Top Trade Bodies to Washington Next Week. They're Going to Fight a $30 Billion Tariff.
news.excerpt: FICCI, CII, the Commerce Ministry and three industry associations will testify before the USTR on July 8, arguing that America's forced-labour findings are legally flawed and economically destructive.
news.image_caption: The Winder Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the Office of the United States Trade Representative
news.nri_angle: If the 12.5% tariff takes effect, it could raise prices on Indian goods in the US, disrupt supply chains that employ diaspora professionals, and complicate the bilateral trade deal that affects everything from H-1B policies to student visa reciprocity.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The RBI Just Handed India's Government Its Biggest Cheque Ever. Here's Why It Matters.
news.excerpt: A record ₹2.87 lakh crore dividend — earned largely from defending the rupee during the Iran war — has compressed India's fiscal deficit to just 9.6% of the full-year target in two months. But the real test lies ahead.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
news.nri_angle: India's fiscal health directly affects rupee stability, bond yields and the investment climate that NRIs navigate for remittances, property and portfolio decisions.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Canada Is Spending $500 Billion on Defence. It Wants India to Help Build the Arsenal.
news.excerpt: From expelled diplomats to a full defence dialogue in four months — Canada and India are engineering one of the fastest diplomatic turnarounds in recent memory, with a free trade deal and a Modi visit to Ottawa on the horizon.
news.image_caption: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who has spearheaded a dramatic reset in India-Canada relations since taking office
news.nri_angle: The India-Canada reset directly affects nearly two million Indian-Canadians through improved visa processing, trade corridors, security cooperation and the political normalisation of a relationship that had turned hostile under Trudeau.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's First Private Rocket Is Ten Days From Orbit. The Startup Behind It Just Became a Unicorn.
news.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace has set a July 12 launch window for Vikram-1, aiming to become only the fourth private company in the world to place a satellite in orbit from its own launch vehicle.
news.image_caption: Skyroot's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh at Sriharikota in November 2022
news.nri_angle: Indian space startups are opening a new pathway for diaspora investors and technologists to participate in India's $44 billion commercial space economy.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Shah Rukh Khan Opens America’s First Franchise-Built Cricket Stadium in Los Angeles
news.excerpt: The $21 million Knight Riders Cricket Ground hosted its inaugural MLC match and will serve as a venue for cricket’s return to the Olympics in 2028
news.image_caption: Shah Rukh Khan, co-owner of the Knight Riders Group, inaugurated the Knight Riders Cricket Ground in Los Angeles on July 1, 2026.
news.nri_angle: For 4.8 million Indian Americans who grew up watching cricket, the first franchise-owned cricket stadium in LA built by Bollywood icon SRK marks a milestone ahead of cricket’s 2028 Olympic return.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: While America Fights Its Data Centers, India Is Rolling Out the Red Carpet. The Numbers Are Staggering.
news.excerpt: Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon are pouring tens of billions into Indian data centers. Zero taxes until 2047, no public hearings, and tenfold capacity growth projected over the next decade.
news.image_caption: Inside a modern data center server room with rows of computing infrastructure
news.nri_angle: Indian-Americans in tech work at the very companies now investing billions in India's data-center infrastructure — the buildout creates jobs, deepens the US-India tech partnership, and opens new investment opportunities from Lightstorm's IPO to semiconductor JVs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The US Is About to End a 30-Year Student Visa Rule. No Country Has More at Stake Than India.
news.excerpt: A proposed rule eliminating 'Duration of Status' would cap F-1 stays at four years, slash grace periods, and threaten the Day-1 CPT pathway that thousands of Indian graduates depend on.
news.image_caption: International students at an American university campus
news.nri_angle: Indian students are 48% of all OPT participants in the US; the rule change could upend the F-1-to-H-1B pipeline that hundreds of thousands of Indian graduates depend on.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Factories Are Cooling Off. The Warning Signs Are Hard to Ignore.
news.excerpt: Manufacturing growth slipped to its second-weakest pace in four years in June, with export orders at a 39-month low and hiring at its softest this year — even as KPIT Technologies crashed 17% on a European demand shock.
news.image_caption: Workers on a production line at an Indian manufacturing facility
news.nri_angle: NRI investors should note that India's manufacturing momentum is fading even as equity valuations remain elevated; European demand weakness impacts IT and engineering outsourcing sectors that employ many diaspora professionals.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Asia's AI Bubble Just Popped. India Barely Flinched.
news.excerpt: South Korea's KOSPI crashed 8% and foreign investors dumped $137 billion from Asian stocks in six months. India rose. Here's why the rotation may be just beginning.
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, home of the Sensex index
news.nri_angle: NRI investors with US-based 401(k) and brokerage exposure to South Korean and Taiwanese tech ETFs face a direct portfolio rotation question as India emerges as the safer alternative.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Federal Judge Called Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee an Illegal Tax. The White House Is Fighting Back.
news.excerpt: The ruling could reshape the economics of hiring foreign workers in America. Indian physicians, engineers, and their employers are caught in the legal crossfire.
news.image_caption: A United States federal courthouse, where the H-1B fee ruling was decided
news.nri_angle: The $100,000 fee directly affects the roughly 400,000 Indian-origin H-1B holders in the US, their employers, and anyone considering a job change or new petition.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The USISPF Summit Honoured Three Business Titans. Sunil Mittal Used His Speech to Talk About Five Million Indians Instead.
nri-world.excerpt: At the IX USISPF Leadership Summit in Washington, Bharti's chairman and India's ambassador to the US laid out a vision in which the diaspora is not a footnote to the India-US partnership but the load-bearing wall.
nri-world.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal, founder and chairman of Bharti Enterprises
nri-world.nri_angle: Mittal explicitly framed the 5-million-strong Indian American community as the strategic bridge between India and the US — in trade, defence, and high technology. Ambassador Kwatra's $30 trillion roadmap positions the diaspora as investors, knowledge partners, and connectors in India's climb to developed-nation status by 2047.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Sitharaman Took India's Chequebook to France. She Is Ending the Trip by Meeting the Diaspora.
nri-world.excerpt: India's finance minister co-chaired an economic dialogue in Aix-en-Provence, courted BNP Paribas and a cargo airship startup, and will wrap up her four-day visit with a community event for Indians in France — the quiet end of a loud trip.
nri-world.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during a European engagement in 2025
nri-world.nri_angle: Sitharaman's France visit concludes with a diaspora community interaction, connecting India's economic diplomacy directly to the 30,000-strong Indian community in France. India-France trade has doubled in a decade to €13.59 billion, and the India-EU FTA signed in January 2026 opens new pathways for NRIs across Europe.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Immigrants Have Built 96 Billion-Dollar Startups in America. No Other Country Comes Close.
nri-world.excerpt: A new NFAP study finds India is the largest source of immigrant unicorn founders in the US, with 96 companies collectively worth more than Germany's stock market.
nri-world.image_caption: Jyoti Bansal, Indian-born founder of AppDynamics and Harness, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2024 — one of 96 Indian immigrant-founded US unicorn startups identified in the NFAP study (Photo: TechCrunch/Katelyn Tucker, CC BY 2.0)
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-born entrepreneurs account for 96 of America's 775 unicorns — the most of any country. Most arrived as IIT graduates on student visas, building the exact pipeline now threatened by tightening H-1B and student visa policies.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Carnegie Names Four Indian Americans to Its 'Great Immigrants' List — on the Eve of America's 250th Birthday
nri-world.excerpt: Nikesh Arora, Mahzarin Banaji, Sanjiv Chopra, and Reshma Kewalramani join a class of 25 naturalized citizens honoured by the Carnegie Corporation for the Fourth of July.
nri-world.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, one of four Indian Americans named to Carnegie's 2026 Great Immigrants list
nri-world.nri_angle: Four Indian-born leaders — spanning cybersecurity, social psychology, medicine, and biotech — are honoured as 'Great Americans' at a moment when immigration restrictions are tightening. The recognition underscores the diaspora's institutional reach across American life.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: New US Bill Would End OPT, Kill H-1B Green Card Pathway in Sweeping Overhaul
nri-world.excerpt: Rep. Chip Roy’s American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act targets every stage of the Indian professional immigration pipeline, from student work permits to permanent residency
nri-world.image_caption: The US Capitol, where Rep. Chip Roy introduced the American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act of 2026 targeting the H-1B visa program.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indians hold 72% of H-1B visas and rely on OPT and the H-1B-to-green-card pipeline that this bill would dismantle — a direct threat to the immigration pathway used by hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Two Thousand Indian-Origin Doctors Just Took Over Tampa's Waterfront. The Timing Was Not an Accident.
nri-world.excerpt: AAPI's 44th annual convention opens on America's 250th birthday weekend, blending scientific sessions with a red-carpet civic reception from the City of Tampa.
nri-world.image_caption: Healthcare professionals in a hospital setting — Indian-origin physicians form one of the largest ethnic groups in American medicine
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin physicians form one of the largest ethnic groups in American medicine. AAPI's convention, timed to America's 250th, is both a professional assembly and a statement of belonging.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Nine Hundred Young Jains Just Sold Out a Convention in New Jersey. Their Theme: 'The Art of the In-Between.'
nri-world.excerpt: The 17th biennial Young Jains of America convention opens this week with 915 attendees across three age cohorts — every spot taken, every waitlist full.
nri-world.image_caption: Jain community celebrations at a temple in New York City
nri-world.nri_angle: Young Jain Americans navigate between an ancient faith built on non-violence and non-attachment and a consumer culture that runs on the opposite. YJA's sold-out convention is the infrastructure they built for that in-between.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Just Killed the Physical OCI Booklet. Five Million Cardholders Can Finally Exhale.
nri-world.excerpt: The new e-OCI card lets overseas Indians complete the entire OCI lifecycle on a phone — no consular visits, no duplicate paperwork, no reissue anxiety.
nri-world.image_caption: Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who launched the e-OCI Card system in New Delhi
nri-world.nri_angle: Eliminates the single biggest bureaucratic pain point for 5M+ OCI holders worldwide — the mandatory physical booklet reissue that required consular visits, mailed documents, and weeks of waiting every time a passport was renewed.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Leicester's South Asian Arts Festival Turns Fifteen. The City Barely Notices — It Has Been Living This for Decades.
nri-world.excerpt: An Indian Summer returns to Leicester Cathedral, Jubilee Square, and Attenborough Arts Centre this week with five days of theatre, music, film, and dance.
nri-world.image_caption: Leicester's Belgrave Road area, known as the 'Golden Mile' — the cultural heart of one of Britain's most prominent South Asian communities
nri-world.nri_angle: Highlights how Leicester's concentrated South Asian diaspora sustains a 15-year-old contemporary arts festival — a model for diaspora cultural institutions that create shared physical space for identity beyond streaming and WhatsApp groups.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Supreme Court Just Ruled 6-3 That Children of H-1B Parents Born in America Are Citizens. No President Can Change That.
nri-world.excerpt: In a landmark ruling, the conservative-majority court struck down Trump's executive order targeting birthright citizenship — a decision that Indian American advocacy groups are calling 'a profound affirmation of who belongs in America.'
nri-world.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court in Washington, D.C.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian families on H-1B and L-1 visas, who face the longest green card backlogs in the system, now have Supreme Court confirmation that their U.S.-born children's citizenship is constitutionally protected.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: America Turns 250. The Indian Diaspora Is Celebrating with Both Flags.
nri-world.excerpt: From a packed curtain raiser in Mineola to a tall ship in Baltimore Harbour, Indian Americans are weaving their story into the semiquincentennial — while already rehearsing for India's 80th.
nri-world.image_caption: The annual India Day Parade in New York City — Indian Americans celebrate their dual identity as America marks its 250th (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: The Indian-American community is uniquely positioned this summer, celebrating America's 250th birthday while preparing for India's 80th Independence Day — a dual-calendar life that defines the diaspora experience.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Bay Area Temples Hit in Three Weeks. The Diaspora Is Running Out of Cheeks to Turn.
nri-world.excerpt: Pro-Khalistan graffiti at a Swaminarayan mandir, a copycat attack in Hayward, and a burglary at a third temple have shaken Silicon Valley's Indian-American heartland — and renewed a question the community has never been able to put down.
nri-world.image_caption: A BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in California, similar to the temples targeted in the Bay Area attacks
nri-world.nri_angle: The Bay Area temple attacks strike at the heart of the Indian-American community's sense of belonging — raising the question of whether success and visibility have made the diaspora a target rather than a shield.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: A Weak US Jobs Report Just Took a Fed Rate Hike Off the Table — and India's Markets Are Surging on the News
markets-finance.excerpt: Nonfarm payrolls came in at just 57,000 against expectations of 115,000, sending the dollar to its biggest one-day drop in two months and pushing Indian equities back above the $5 trillion mark for the first time since the Iran crisis began.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai — India's equity market has reclaimed the $5 trillion valuation mark
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with US-denominated earnings and India-allocated portfolios benefit directly from a weaker dollar and easing Fed rate fears — the macro backdrop for Indian equities is the most favourable it has been in months.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's IT Giants Face Their Most Scrutinised Earnings Season in Years — and AI Is the Elephant in Every Boardroom
markets-finance.excerpt: With the Nifty IT index down 33% from its February peak, TCS and Infosys are about to report June-quarter results that could determine whether the sector's correction is a buying opportunity or the start of a structural decline.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bangalore — India's IT bellwether reports Q1 FY27 results on July 23
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors hold significant IT sector exposure and many work in the very industry under scrutiny — this earnings season is both a portfolio and career signal.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Wall Street Just Raised India's Growth Forecast to 7% — the Sharpest Upward Revision in Over a Year
markets-finance.excerpt: Bank of America, Crisil, and Goldman Sachs have all upgraded India's outlook in the span of a week, citing collapsing oil prices, the Iran peace deal, and a capex surge — while the rupee posts its first quarterly gain since early 2025
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai — the central bank's dollar-inflow measures have helped the rupee post its first quarterly gain in over a year
markets-finance.nri_angle: Rupee stability means NRI equity and debt returns are no longer being eroded by currency depreciation; the wave of growth upgrades improves the case for India-linked portfolio allocations.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is 'Very, Very Close' to a Historic US Trade Deal — but a $500 Billion Target and New Tariffs Stand in the Way
markets-finance.excerpt: As the India-UK CETA prepares to launch on July 15, Washington says a bilateral trade agreement with New Delhi is nearly done — while a proposed 12.5% forced-labour tariff threatens to complicate the final stretch
markets-finance.image_caption: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds sign the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
markets-finance.nri_angle: A US deal could lower tariff costs on Indian exports and ease barriers for IT professionals, while the UK CETA eliminates double social security payments for NRIs in Britain
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's SIP Investors Refuse to Blink — ₹30,000 Crore a Month Keeps Flowing Even as Equity Fund Inflows Drop 40%
markets-finance.excerpt: Systematic investment plans held above ₹30,000 crore for three straight months through May 2026, absorbing a sharp lump-sum pullback and underlining a structural shift in how Indian retail money behaves.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Phiroze Jeejeebhoy Towers, home of the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors who use SIP channels to invest in Indian mutual funds should note that the domestic retail floor is now structurally strong enough to cushion FII selling — a dynamic that reduces the kind of sharp drawdowns that used to punish long-distance investors.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Emerging as Asia's Safe Haven as the Global AI Selloff Crushes South Korea and Taiwan
markets-finance.excerpt: With KOSPI plunging below 8,000 and foreigners dumping $137 billion of Asian equities in H1 2026, India's oil-fuelled rally and domestic-demand story are pulling global money in a new direction
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, home of the Sensex
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with Asian market exposure face a historic rotation away from AI-heavy chip plays in Korea and Taiwan toward India, where oil collapse, rupee recovery, and domestic-demand sectors offer a compelling alternative.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is About to Witness Its Biggest-Ever IPO Wave — From Jio's $3.8 Billion Listing to Carlsberg's Beer Play
markets-finance.excerpt: Carlsberg has confidentially filed for a $700 million India IPO, joining a pipeline that includes Jio Platforms, NSE, PhonePe, and Pernod Ricard — collectively the largest collection of marquee listings India has ever seen in a single year
markets-finance.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India, set to host what could be the country's biggest IPO wave
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors who can access Indian IPOs through demat accounts or GIFT City–routed platforms face a once-in-a-generation lineup — but the sheer volume of issuance will test whether the market can absorb it all.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Households Just Sold 50 Tonnes of Gold in a Single Quarter — the Sharpest Spike in Years
markets-finance.excerpt: Nearly 50 tonnes of old gold flooded back into the market in April–June 2026, a 43% jump from a year ago. For a nation that treats gold as heirloom, the shift from hoarding to liquidating signals something deeper than just falling prices.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold jewellery: Antique Indian Nose Ring Jewellery
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI families holding gold in India face rebalancing decisions as prices drop 22% from peak; the shift from physical hoarding to digital gold instruments reshapes how diaspora investors should think about gold in their Indian portfolio.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: KPIT Technologies Just Lost 17% in a Single Day — and 6 Lakh Retail Investors Are Caught in the Wreckage
markets-finance.excerpt: The Pune-based auto software company's surprise profit warning, driven by sudden European OEM spending cuts, triggers JPMorgan downgrade and drags peers Tata Elxsi and LTTS down with it — a cautionary tale for NRI investors in India's mid-cap IT story
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock trading screen showing market data — KPIT Technologies shares crashed 17% to a near four-year low on July 1, 2026
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to Indian mid-cap IT mutual funds are directly affected — KPIT's crash reveals the concentration risk in thematic auto-tech bets and raises questions about whether the broader Indian IT services sector faces structural headwinds from European demand weakness and AI disruption
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's GST Collections Just Surged 14% to ₹1.95 Lakh Crore — but Imports Are Doing the Heavy Lifting
markets-finance.excerpt: June's headline growth looks robust, but a 34.6% surge in import revenues is masking modest 6.5% domestic growth. The divergence tells a nuanced story about where India's economy actually stands.
markets-finance.image_caption: A government official addresses a GST Town Hall meeting in Bengaluru
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors should note the domestic GST growth of just 6.5% — well below the headline 14% — as a signal that India's consumption engine may need more time before justifying premium market valuations.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Oil Just Posted Its Steepest Quarterly Drop Since 2020 — and India May Be the Biggest Winner
markets-finance.excerpt: Brent crude has crashed 43% from its Iran war peak to $71 a barrel, erasing the entire geopolitical risk premium. For the world's third-largest oil importer, the implications for inflation, the rupee, and the fiscal balance are enormous.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Essar Oil Refinery in Gujarat — India imports nearly 90% of its crude, making it one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global oil price crash
markets-finance.nri_angle: India imports 90% of its crude — the oil crash directly improves the current account, inflation outlook, rupee stability, and investment case that NRI portfolios depend on.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Auto Giants Just Posted Blockbuster June Sales — Maruti Hit a Record 200K Units While Mahindra Surged 37%
markets-finance.excerpt: The country's biggest carmakers reported their strongest June in years, led by an SUV boom and rising exports — but a historically dry monsoon and looming El Niño threaten the rural demand that sustains the volume story
markets-finance.image_caption: A Maruti Suzuki car — the market leader sold a record 200,390 units in June 2026
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian auto stocks are among the most widely held by NRI investors — and the monsoon-versus-premiumization question will shape sector returns for the rest of FY27
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Five Teams, Six Points, and the Tightest MLC Race American Cricket Has Ever Seen
sports.excerpt: MI New York's five-run win over Seattle has left five of six franchises level on points with the playoffs a fortnight away. For NRIs across America, the sport they grew up with has never felt closer.
sports.image_caption: Grand Prairie Stadium, one of MLC's home venues in the Dallas–Fort Worth area
sports.nri_angle: MLC matches are being played in cities with large Indian tech communities — Redmond, Grand Prairie, Pomona, Fairfax — putting competitive T20 cricket within driving distance of NRIs across America.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Sumit Nagal Ends a Two-Year Title Drought in Romania. India's No. 1 Says He Questioned Everything.
sports.excerpt: The 28-year-old from Haryana, who fell from world No. 68 to No. 297, beat France's Felix Balshaw in the Intaro Open final for his seventh Challenger title. He says the hardest battle was against himself.
sports.image_caption: Sumit Nagal at the 2022 French Open qualifying rounds

lifestyle-health.title: Your Teen's Friends May Shape Their Mental Health More Than You Think — A 600,000-Person Study Shows How

lifestyle-health.title: Fish Oil Supplements Don't Protect Your Brain From Alzheimer's, a Rigorous Two-Year Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Americans spend over $1 billion a year on fish oil, but a USC clinical trial shows the supplements fail to slow cognitive decline — even though they reach the brain. For South Asians, the findings raise uncomfortable questions about a supplement many families swear by.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fish oil capsules, among the most popular dietary supplements worldwide
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face rising Alzheimer's risk and are heavy fish oil users — this trial suggests they should shift spending from supplements to whole-food diets.

lifestyle-health.title: Remote Work Is Making Americans Lonelier and More Depressed — and the Effect Is Worst for Those Who Live Alone
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A sweeping study of 588,000 workers finds that the shift to working from home accounts for a third of the rise in national mental distress since 2011. For Indian-origin tech workers thousands of miles from family, the findings hit close to home.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A remote worker at a home desk — the daily reality for millions in tech and knowledge-economy roles
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech workers in the US are disproportionately in remotable jobs and far from family — making them especially vulnerable to the isolation the study documents.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Older Adults Who Walk Like Someone 30 Years Younger Have Half the Risk of Cognitive Decline — Even With Alzheimer's Pathology
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark study in Neurology identifies 'super movers' — people over 80 whose brisk gait appears to shield their brains from dementia, offering a deceptively simple biomarker that diaspora families can track as parents age
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older adult walking briskly through a park — a habit that new research links to sharply lower dementia risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated diabetes and cardiovascular risk that accelerate cognitive decline; walking speed is a culturally familiar, measurable biomarker diaspora families can track as parents age.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Three to Four Cups of Coffee a Day Can Halve Your Risk of Liver Cancer — and Decaf Works Too
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 354,957-person Cedars-Sinai study finds that moderate coffee drinking — regular or decaf — is linked to dramatically lower rates of cirrhosis, liver cancer and liver-related death, with implications for South Asians facing rising fatty liver disease
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A freshly brewed cup of coffee — moderate daily consumption has been linked to significantly lower liver cancer and cirrhosis risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face rising NAFLD rates — moderate coffee drinking may offer a simple protective intervention aligned with India's filter coffee tradition
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Just 12 Weeks of Time-Restricted Eating Can Keep Weight Off for a Full Year, a New Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A randomised trial from Spain shows that limiting meals to an eight-hour window produces durable weight loss regardless of whether you eat early or late — a flexible strategy that could reshape how South Asians manage obesity.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh vegetables and fruits arranged for healthy meal planning — a visual representation of time-restricted eating. (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest rates of metabolic syndrome globally, and a flexible, no-calorie-counting approach to weight management that fits around family mealtimes or shift-work schedules could prove especially practical for diaspora households.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.image_caption: A bowl of brightly coloured ultra-processed breakfast cereal, a typical NOVA Group 4 food
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Diaspora Indians transitioning from traditional home-cooked food to Western ultra-processed diets face compounded gastrointestinal cancer risk on top of already elevated metabolic disease rates.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Turmeric's Active Compound Can Ease Depression as Effectively as Some Drugs — and the Evidence Is Growing

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For NRIs choosing between US cities and suburbs, this study offers data-backed guidance: walkable, green neighborhoods don't just feel better — they measurably protect your physical and mental health.

lifestyle-health.title: Millennials and Gen X Are Aging Faster Biologically Than Their Parents — and a Major Study Links It to Rising Cancer Rates
